name: _sparse_mask_projection
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::_sparse_mask_projection(Tensor self, Tensor mask, bool accumulate_matches=False) -> Tensor. This overload is the representative contract only; it is not the complete contract and is not exclusive. The original Gems pytest defines the full overload, keyword-argument, return, error, aliasing and mutation behavior, including the other registered overload aten::_sparse_mask_projection.out(Tensor self, Tensor mask, bool accumulate_matches=False, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!), which takes a keyword-only out buffer, mutates it, and returns it aliased to out (the tests assert res_ret is out). Do not narrow the tests to this signature, and never remove tests or adapt reference behavior to fit this one signature. Semantics derived from the tests: the operator intersects two COO sparse tensors that share one size() and one sparse_dim and returns a COO tensor storing exactly the entries stored in self; a stored entry whose coordinate is also stored in mask keeps its value, every other stored entry is zeroed, and coordinates stored only in mask are dropped. Mask values are never truth conditions: stored coordinates alone select entries. The result's stored order, coalesced flag and dtype mirror self, and accumulate_matches=True adds self's value once per matching stored mask entry, which is a plain copy unless the mask repeats a coordinate. Both operands must be COO; dense self, dense mask, size mismatch, sparse_dim mismatch, a non-bool accumulate_matches (the tests probe a string value) and a dense out buffer all raise, and the native operator has no autograd formula. Registered schemas, verbatim: aten::_sparse_mask_projection(Tensor self, Tensor mask, bool accumulate_matches=False) -> Tensor ; aten::_sparse_mask_projection.out(Tensor self, Tensor mask, bool accumulate_matches=False, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!)
